metadata.title: From Coordinates to Invariants in a Two-Dimensional Worldsheet Quark Model: Quotient Geometry, Lattice Index Stress Tests, and a Bottomonium Falsification
metadata.description:
Abstract

A two-dimensional worldsheet quark model (2DQM) can be made substantially sharper by replacing coordinate- and convention-dependent expressions with a minimal set of invariants defined relative to explicit transformation groups. We perform that reduction and then attempt to falsify the surviving structure. The original bosonic sector is compressed into a quotient parameter, geometric/moduli data, Lorentz-Gram structure, a discrete topological sector, an oscillator-algebra class, and a normalized spectral fingerprint. We distinguish removable coefficients (I0), continuous moduli (I1), discrete/topological invariants (I2), and critical/discriminant coordinates (I3), and use reconstructibility as the criterion for redundancy. In synthetic and lattice stress tests, an explicit two-dimensional U(1) Wilson-overlap construction reproduced the oriented topological degree for every tested sector d=-3,...,3 and remained unchanged under local gauge transformations. A topology-changing interpolation produced an index jump only at near-closure of the Wilson-kernel gap (grid estimate t≈0.5105), providing a concrete discriminant event. We then locked an external primary test to the Particle Data Group 2026 Upsilon(1S)-Upsilon(4S) masses and tested the exact affine mass-squared law implied by the reduced spectral branch. The model was decisively rejected (chi-square=70359.15, df=2); the unit-free ratios were R3=1.6162 and R4=2.0443 versus linear-law targets 2 and 3, and adjacent mass-squared spacings decreased from 10.969 to 6.760 to 4.696 GeV^2. Approximately 38.4% intrinsic fractional scatter in adjacent mass-squared spacing would be required to make a constant-spacing description statistically commensurate with these four states. Thus the invariant-reduction machinery survives the tested mathematical nuisance transformations, whereas the exact affine hadron-spectrum submodel does not. The proposed identification of flavor with topological degree remains unestablished and is not claimed.

Keywords: invariants; quotient geometry; algebraic geometry; worldsheet; lattice Dirac operator; topological index; bottomonium; falsification; spectral reconstructibility

metadata.title: The Kaleidoscopic Foundation of the Universe Unifying Quantum Mechanics, Spacetime, and Thermodynamics via Combinatorial Logic
metadata.description: This work defines a unified scientific framework in which continuous spacetime is not a fundamental postulate, but an emergent property from the discrete combinatorics of purified integer partitions. Leveraging the \textit{Universal Kaleidoscopic Filter Theorem}, the text provides the algebraic foundations based on Weyl reflections, alongside conceptual analogies to intuitively grasp the origin of space, time, and relativistic causality. Furthermore, this definitive version geometrically derives Planck's quantum of action, resolves the objective wavefunction collapse, explains the Yang-Mills mass gap, demonstrates matter-antimatter asymmetry, rigorously derives the Holographic Principle, uncovers the geometric origins of Spin-Statistics and Quantum Entanglement, and provides exact topological solutions for Quantum Gravity renormalizability, Standard Model Gauge Symmetries, the Hierarchy Problem, the Dark Sector, the Ultimate Cosmological Destiny of the Universe, and the Geometric Resolution of the Riemann Hypothesis, rendering the theory unassailable against all relativistic and quantum-mechanical critiques.

metadata.title: Quantum Spin and Angular Momentum: Formal Structure Experimental Foundations and Open Questions
metadata.description: This paper presents a comprehensive survey of quantum spin and angular momentum, tracing their theoretical roots, experimental confirmations, and current frontiers. It covers the formal mathematical structure of spin using SU(2) symmetry, Pauli matrices, and commutation relations, and explores how these constructs underlie observable phenomena like Zeeman splitting, Stern–Gerlach results, and spin-orbit coupling. The paper also examines spin in the context of relativistic quantum mechanics (via the Dirac equation), entanglement, and quantum field theory. Critical experiments—such as electron g-factor measurements, muon spin resonance, and neutron interferometry—are reviewed. A significant focus is given to unresolved issues: the spin-statistics connection, the measurement problem, spin in curved spacetime, and the possibility of sub-quantum spin structures or deeper geometric origins. This work serves as both a foundational reference and an open invitation to rethink spin’s role in the quantum universe, especially in light of emerging field-based theories.

metadata.description: Quantum spin emerges as the angular harmonic structure of brane-bulk wave modes at focal deceleration zones. Half-integer spin arises from the topological double-cover of SO(3) — wave functions return to their original state only after 4pi rotation, a consequence of the auxetic brane geometry (nu=-1) and G2 automorphism group structure. The NMR/MRI analogy is structural and not merely pedagogical: brane spin modes precess under sump gradients exactly as nuclear spins precess in a B0 field, with the gyromagnetic ratio gamma mapping to the sump coupling constant. The T1/T2/T2 relaxation hierarchy maps directly onto spin dynamics — T1 governs return to sump equilibrium (spin-lattice), T2 governs cluster dephasing (spin-spin), and T2 governs coherent BH focal zone precession. This provides the physical foundation for the MRI analogy used throughout the series. Spin-statistics connection: bosons (integer spin) are even angular harmonics of the brane; fermions (half-integer) are odd harmonics requiring double-cover topology. Part of the One Octonion brane-bulk series (Papers I-XL), anchor DOI:10.5281/zenodo.19120873.

metadata.title: Paper VIII: Quantum Spin as Angular Harmonics of the Brane Wave Modes
metadata.description:
Quantum spin is proposed to be the angular harmonic structure of the brane-bulk wave modes at focal deceleration zones. Electric charge is the radial mode (Paper VI); spin is the angular mode of the same wave. Half-integer spin (s = 1/2) arises from the requirement that the angular wave function return to its original state after a 4π rotation of the brane (a topological double-cover of SO(3)). Integer spin (s = 0, 1, 2...) corresponds to wave modes that close after 2π rotation. The spin-statistics theorem follows: half-integer spinors (fermions) are the fundamental matter constituents; integer- spin modes (bosons) are force carriers. The NMR/MRI analogy is structural: the brane spin modes precess under external sump gradients exactly as nuclear spins precess in a magnetic eld, with the T1/T2/T2* relaxation hierarchy governing the dephasing dynamics.

Part of the One-Octonion Brane-Bulk Framework series. Anchor DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19120873. Community: one-octonion-brane-bulk. Author: Bharathi Dasan Jagadeesan, M.D., University of Minnesota. ORCID: 0000-0002-1143-941X.

metadata.title: Emergent Relativistic Spacetime and Lorentz Invariance via the Universal Kaleidoscopic Filter on Integer Partitions
metadata.description: This paper establishes a rigorous, comprehensive theoretical framework wherein continuous relativistic spacetime, causal structure, and Lorentz invariance are derived not as fundamental, irreducible axioms, but as emergent thermodynamic limits of the discrete combinatorics of purified integer partitions. By executing the Kaleidoscopic Filter Theorem, we prove that the systematic application of alternating Weyl reflection operators to unrestricted partition lattices entirely annihilates lower-dimensional topological boundary noise and metric singularities. This mathematical sieve yields an interior log-concave core characterized by strict structural rigidity. The macroscopic speed of light $c$ is rigorously derived as a maximum algorithmic processing rate governing state transitions between contiguous Weyl chambers. Furthermore, we provide a complete treatment of high-energy Lorentz symmetry breaking at the Planck scale, deriving a modified dispersion relation and introducing a Hopf-algebraic deformation of the Poincar\'e algebra to show how causality is preserved under non-linear representations. We extend the formalism to prove that Gauge symmetries, the Yang-Mills mass gap, the Spin-Statistics theorem, the Geometric Origin of Inertia, and the Einstein Field Equations are strictly geometric consequences of this discrete architecture. We conclude with precise, testable cosmological predictions regarding photon dispersion and the Dark Sector, rendering this unified model strictly falsifiable.
